newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - Brazil cellular selloff to rake in billions.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Brazil cellular selloff to rake in billions.

text.p: Brazil will reap hundreds of millions of reais more than the 3.7 billion-real base price it set on Monday for opening its promising cellular telephone sector to foreign capital, investment banking analysts said.
"If the government sells all 10 concessions, it could get a total of five billion reais," said Maxim Medvedovsky, an analyst with local bank Banco Icatu.

Competition will be stiff March 31 when some 20 consortia are expected to submit bids for B Band concessions across Brazil in a privatization that has caught the eye of nearly every major global telecoms operator, analysts said.

The minimum concession prices were released Monday by the Communications Ministry in four phone book-sized bid documents. The prices, which were within market expectations, were seen as the only major news to come out of the tender specifications.
Although the documents brought no major surprises, analysts said their release was a positive development, setting Brazil firmly on the path toward privatizing its telecoms sector.
"Now we are really on the road to privatization," said Eduardo Munemori, a telecoms analyst at local bank Banco Pactual. "It will be very hard to turn back now."

Brazil set base prices of 600 million reais each for concessions for metropolitan Sao Paulo and Sao Paulo state while a contract for Rio de Janeiro and Espiritu Santo states had a base price of 500 million reais. Each of the other seven concessions have lower base prices; collectively they add up to about 2 billion reais.

"They are about what was expected but we are definitely going to see higher bids, especially for Rio and Sao Paulo," said Medvedovsky, adding fierce bidding may push the purchase price for the two Sao Paulo concessions to as high as 2.0 billion reais.
Although analysts said the Rio and Sao Paulo prices seemed low, base prices for concessions serving Brazil's larger but more sparsely populated north and northeast were higher than some had expected.
Winners of the bids will be required to install some 11.1 million new cellular lines, including 3.6 million new lines in the two Sao Paulo concession areas.
Although the government did not give a time frame for meeting the line requirements, analysts said the number seemed a little high.
"It is very ambitious so we have to see what the deadline will be," said Sergio Missima, an analyst with local bank Banco Fator.
Pent-up demand in the city and state of Sao Paulo is estimated at two million lines, but that could rise sharply if cellular prices fall, he said.
"If you lower the price, you'll raise demand," Missima said.
The bid specifications said 40 percent of the purchase price must be paid at the time the contract is signed with the remaining 60 percent paid in three equal, annual installments.
Most analysts said the requirement is positive for consortia, which had expected to pay at least 50 percent of the price up front.
